runs.title: Carson Wentz starts for the Vikings: the club's word
runs.prompt: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray is reportedly injured and Carson Wentz is expected to start the Monday Night Football game against the Buffalo Bills on 10 November 2026. Find out whether Wentz is confirmed as the starter and exactly what the Vikings (or the NFL) have said about Kyler Murray's injury and timeline. Look for the club's or league's own statement, not just rumor.
runs.answer: Yes — confirmed by the club itself, not just rumor. In a vikings.com news story on Nov 5, 2026, Head Coach Kevin O'Connell announced Carson Wentz will start the Monday Night Football game against Buffalo, with Max Brosmer as backup. On Murray, O'Connell said: "After evaluating Kyler on Monday, getting some imagery and things, we did determine he does have a hamstring strain. We don't believe it to be more than a week-to-week kind of thing right now," adding that playing him early risked "turning this into a more significant injury." No specific return date was given — only "week to week." That was formalized on the Vikings' official Week 9 injury report: Murray (hamstring) did not practice Thursday, Friday or Saturday and is listed OUT; Wentz is not on the report at all. Note the game is Week 9 at U.S. Bank Stadium, Minneapolis, on Monday Nov 9, 2026 ET — which is the early hours of 10 November in UK/European time.

runs.title: Ryanair's new 60-minute baggage rule: the details
runs.prompt: Ryanair is introducing a new rule from around 10 November 2026 where airport bag drop for checked luggage closes 60 minutes before departure. Find out exactly what the new rule is, from when it takes effect, and what Ryanair's own corporate/official page says about it. A traveller wants to know how this changes how early they must arrive.
runs.answer: From Tuesday 10 November 2026, Ryanair's airport check-in and bag drop desks close 60 minutes before scheduled departure, up from 40 minutes today — Ryanair says the extra 20 minutes is to give passengers more time to clear security and passport queues and reach the gate on time, cutting the small number of people who miss flights in queues. The help-centre FAQ confirms it affects only the ~20% of passengers with checked bags (over 80% travel cabin-bag only and are unaffected), and check-in desks/staff remain, with self-service kiosks at 95%+ of airports by October. Ryanair's standing arrival advice is unchanged: be at the check-in/bag drop desk at least 2 hours before departure and at the boarding gate at least 30 minutes before departure — so a bag-dropping traveller who currently cuts it fine at ~60–70 minutes before departure must now plan the full 2 hours, while those arriving at the recommended 2 hours see no practical change.

runs.title: England's school phone ban: what it covers
runs.prompt: The UK government has announced stricter rules banning phones from pupils' bags or pockets in schools in England. Find out what the new policy actually says: what exactly is banned, when it applies, and who it covers. Prefer the official GOV.UK guidance page and confirm the key details from there.
runs.answer: The official DfE statutory guidance (mobile phones in schools) currently requires every school to be a "mobile phone-free environment by default": policies must prohibit phone use throughout the school day — lessons, time between lessons, breaktime and lunchtime — and DfE says pupils should "not have access to their mobile phone" in that time, with BYOD schemes excluding phones and headteachers free to choose how (lockers, pouches, collection). It applies to schools and trusts in England of all phases, with boarding/residential schools banning phones only across the teaching day (plus welfare-based rules and private family contact), and sixth-formers possibly allowed limited access in designated areas (never in front of younger pupils); it also covers other smart devices at the school's discretion. This guidance became statutory on 29 June 2026, with schools told to begin following it from 1 September 2026. runs.title: Dai Henwood: confirm the news and the tributes

runs.answer: Confirmed: Dai Henwood died on the morning of 10 November 2026, aged 48, after living with colon cancer for six years (diagnosed publicly in 2023) — reported by 1News ("Comedian Dai Henwood dies aged 48 after six years living with cancer") and Stuff ("Beloved Kiwi comedian Dai Henwood dies aged 48"), with an NZ Herald obituary headlined "Comedian Dai Henwood dies, aged 48, after long battle with colon cancer" and RNZ coverage. He was a founding member of the Three panel show 7 Days (150+ episodes), a stand-up who won the Billy T Award in 2002, host of Dancing with the Stars NZ, Family Feud and LEGO Masters NZ, a Taskmaster NZ contestant, and was made an Officer of the NZ Order of Merit in 2025 for services to entertainment and charity fundraising; he also shared his illness in the 2024 book The Life of Dai (with Jaquie Brown) and the documentary series Live and Let Dai. He is survived by his wife Jo, children Charlie and Lucy, and his mother Dame Carolyn Henwood, and is being remembered for kindness as much as comedy — Rhys Darby said "New Zealand has lost a titan", Melanie Bracewell called him "the kindest, funniest and most generous performer I've ever met", and the 7 Days team,

It states plainly that Murray is out of the Monday Night Football game vs. the Bills with a hamstring strain, that Head Coach Kevin O'Connell announced Carson Wentz will start in his place, and that Max Brosmer is the backup, with O'Connell's quote explaining the team didn't want to risk turning the strain into a more significant injury. NFL.com's version is equally readable and states the same fact and reason, so it works as a backup source; Yahoo Sports is not usable because only the headline and recommended-story links render, not the article body.
